t: Tigranes the Great entered Syria in 83 BCE at the invitation of a faction in its civil wars and ruled it for 17 years, putting the Seleucid Empire virtually at an end.
At its peak Armenia held Iberia, Albania, Cappadocia, Cilicia, Osroene, Adiabene, Syria, Judea and Atropatene, with Parthia and some Arab tribes as Tigranes' vassals.
Armenia became a Roman client kingdom in 66 BCE after Pompey defeated its ally Mithridates VI of Pontus at the Battle of the Lycus; the last Artaxiad kings were overthrown in 12 CE.
dyk: Strabo and Plutarch say Hannibal was received at the court of Artaxias I and, in a story they also tell, planned and supervised the building of Artaxata, though the tale is reckoned apocryphal.
ev: The Seleucids are defeated by Rome at the Battle of Magnesia; in the same year Artaxias I founds a Hellenistic Armenian state, with Zariadres ruling the kingdom of Sophene.
Artaxias I's reign begins; he seizes Yervandashat and unites the Armenian Highlands at the expense of neighbouring tribes.
Artaxias founds Artaxata (Artashat) near the Araxes, at the junction of trade routes linking the Greek world with Bactria, India and the Black Sea.
Tigranes the Great enters Syria and establishes himself as its ruler, ending the Seleucid Empire in all but name.
Rome conquers Tigranes' empire; Armenia's brief imperial period ends.
After Pompey defeats Mithridates VI of Pontus at the Battle of the Lycus, Armenia becomes a Roman client kingdom.
Mark Antony invades and defeats the kingdom; Rome loses its hegemony in the Final War of the Republic of 32–30 BCE.
The last Artaxiad kings are overthrown, suspected of allegiance to Parthia.

f.capital: Artaxata (Artashat), founded 185 BCE; Tigranakert under Tigranes the Great; earlier Yervandashat
f.founder: Artaxias I (Artashes I), a Seleucid commander presumed to have been related to the Orontid dynasty
f.predecessor: The Orontid kingdom of Armenia under Orontes IV, overthrown in 201/200 BCE, within the Seleucid sphere
f.successor: Roman client kings, then the Arsacid dynasty of Armenia from the crowning of Tiridates I
